chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man came to another man. He said: “If he was muḥṣan, then execution is upon him; and if he was not muḥṣan, then the hadd punishment is upon him.”
I said: Then what is upon the one to whom it was done? He said: “Execution is upon him in every case, whether he was muḥṣan or not muḥṣan.”

key_terms.الْقَتْلُ: execution as the prescribed punishment in this context
key_terms.الْمُؤْتَى بِهِ: the one to whom the act was done
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally married or otherwise in a state of iḥṣān in the legal sense

ai.seo_question: What punishment does this hadith prescribe for liwat according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding liwat, distinguishing in one part between the muḥṣan and non-muḥṣan perpetrator, while prescribing execution for the one acted upon in all cases. It belongs to the fiqh discussions of prescribed punishments and reflects the severe legal treatment of this act in Shia hadith literature.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5047 - In the narration reported by Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Abdullah (as), he said: I asked Imam (as) about a man who approached another man (committing sodomy).
Imam (as) replied: "If the perpetrator was married (muhṣan), then his punishment is execution, and if he was not married, then the legal punishment (hadd) applies to him."
I then asked: "What about the one who was approached?"
Imam (as) replied: "He must be executed in all cases, whether he was married or unmarried."
